title: Topological simplification guided by forbidden regions
summary: Topological simplification is the process of reducing complexity of a function while maintaining its essential features. Its goal is to find a new filter function, which reorders cells of the input complex in a way which eliminates some persistent homological features, without affecting the rest. We present a new approach to simplification based on the concept of forbidden regions and combinatorial dynamics.
